issue.title: mac AXE keeps live lumberjacks stale and runner capacity at zero after long uptime
issue.description: PROPOSED BY phase bead sase-x7.2.1.5.1 note #5. During the read-only mac G3 probe on 2026-09-06, sase axe status reported the orchestrator running with a coherent held lock and live PID 94796, but overall state DEGRADED / health UNHEALTHY, runners hooks 0/3 and agents 0/3, and two live lumberjacks (checks PID 94821 and comments PID 94823) in stale_heartbeat for 15m27s after roughly 12h uptime. Other lumberjacks were still ticking, so this is not a stopped orchestrator. Evidence: file:explicit:e3bb4b2a1e2da5cbc7fe3f99. Root cause is unknown; investigate macOS sleep/wake and long-lived supervisor heartbeat/runner-capacity recovery. Distinct from sase-wd, which is a child stdio bad-file-descriptor failure, but plausibly related through long-lived macOS lumberjack recovery.

task_type_fields.impact: Checks and comment lumberjacks stop making progress while AXE remains nominally running; all hook and agent runner capacity is unavailable, so background automation silently degrades until operator recovery.
task_type_fields.location: AXE orchestrator/lumberjack heartbeat and runner supervision on macOS; evidence file:explicit:e3bb4b2a1e2da5cbc7fe3f99
task_type_fields.repro: On mac after a long-lived AXE run spanning normal laptop sleep/wake, run sase axe status. Observed 2026-09-06: coherent live orchestrator PID 94796, checks/comments child PIDs still live but stale_heartbeat for 15m27s, and hook/agent runner capacity both 0/3.
